findings.finding: A task-involving climate supports the basic psychological needs of autonomy, competence, and relatedness.
findings.quote: Perceptions of a task-involving climate were positively associated with satisfaction of the needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness.

findings.finding: Environments that emphasize ego-involving competition are linked to lower rates of long-term participation.
findings.quote: greater ego-involving motivational climate perceptions predicted less likelihood of adherence.

findings.finding: A task-involving climate encourages striving for excellence without the negative pressure of perfectionistic concerns.
findings.quote: perceptions of a task-involving climate in training/performing environments may encourage striving for excellence and perfection without promoting excessive concerns regarding their attainment.

principle: Creating a task-involving environment that focuses on personal growth and effort rather than ego-driven competition improves dancer well-being and long-term adherence.
for_the_teacher: Focus feedback on the learner's personal progress and effort rather than comparing them to others or an ideal standard.
Use language that emphasizes learning and mastery to foster a task-involving climate.
Normalize mistakes as a natural part of the learning process to reduce perfectionistic concerns.
